Subject: Dedicated vs hyperscaler - qualification & next steps

Sam --

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

What we heard:
- Primary workload: embeddings and document summarization for search & chat; peak inference is mostly short responses but occasional long (up to ~2k tokens) generative outputs.
- Traffic shape: steady baseline ~40-60 qps, with peaks ~120 qps during business hours. Need predictable throughput for search queries.
- Main alternatives you're evaluating: reserved GPU capacity on AWS/GCP (dedicated EC2/GPU fleets) vs managed inference APIs. Key asks: capacity guarantees, tail latency (p95), cost visibility, and security controls (SOC2 + data residency).

Redwood differentiators (brief):
- Dedicated capacity with reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput commitments (can be sized to match peak and kept idle for warm caches).
- Smart routing + autoscale policies to give burst capacity while protecting a committed pool.
- Built-in prefix/KV caching to reduce cost on repeated contexts.
- Observable billing and per-token latency breakdowns for cost/quality tradeoffs.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Run a short POC (2 weeks) comparing:
   - Throughput test (sustained qps for your 1k/2k token scenarios)
   - Tail-latency (p95/p99 under load)
   - Failure/fallback behavior (simulate region/capacity loss)
   - Cost snapshot (tokens / GPU-hours during tests)
2) Redwood to supply a sizing estimate and a canary config for a dedicated pool (we'll include recommended kernels/quantization).
3) We'll share a short tech doc + comparison deck and a proposed statement of work for reserved capacity.

I attached: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_comparison.pdf and poc-scope.md (scope + metrics).

Can you confirm: a) the timeframe you prefer for the POC (next two weeks vs late July), and b) who on your side manages procurement/security so we can route SOC2 and contract questions?

Thanks -- happy to sync if you'd prefer a quick 20-min follow-up.

--Markus

Thanks Markus -- that recap matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from my side: 

- The primary comparison will be: 1) our reserved GPU fleet (we're already running inference on reserved EC2/GPU instances) and 2) managed inference APIs from other vendors. Our procurement team is focused on reserved capacity vs managed endpoints because of predictability and cost.
- Our target SLOs: p95 < 200ms for short responses (<=256 tokens) and p95 < 800ms for long responses (~2k tokens). We care a lot about p99 for user-facing chat.
- For the POC we'd prefer the week of July 20 if that works. We need a simple pricing delta for committed capacity vs pay-as-you-go to bring to procurement.

Security/compliance: our security team requires SOC2 documentation and a short note about data retention and KMS/HSM support for keys in transit and at rest.

I'll loop in Emily Chen from procurement once we lock dates (emily.chen@acmecloud.com).

Quick Q: do you offer a short reserved trial (1 month) with a minimum commitment? If so, what are typical contract minimums?

--Sam

Hi Sam --

Thanks for the clarity. Quick technical plan and what we can ship for a POC starting the week of July 20: 

POC outline (2 weeks):
- Week 1: Baseline tests vs your reserved fleet
  - Deploy a dedicated Redwood pool sized to your peak profile (we estimate 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs for sustained 100-120 qps for short requests; see attached sizing_estimates.xlsx).
  - Run synthetic throughput tests for 256-token and 2k-token cases; collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU utilization, and token cost.
- Week 2: Resilience & fallbacks
  - Simulate spike + regional failure to exercise autoscale and fallback to burst capacity (document behavior and observed latency).
  - Test prefix/KV cache hit-rate effect on cost for identical repeated queries.

What we need from Acme:
- Representative request traces (anonymized) or a small corpus to run the similarity/embedding workloads.
- Contact for procurement/security (Sam noted Emily Chen).
- A service account we can use to push test traffic (we'll provide scripts).

Deliverables:
- Test results dashboard + raw metrics
- Cost comparison (GPU-hours + token estimate) vs your current reserved fleet
- Short recommendations (config + rollout path) and a draft reserved-capacity SOW and quote.

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_comparison.pdf, sizing_estimates.xlsx, poc-scope.md

On the reserved trial: yes, we can stand up a short-term reserved pool for a POC. Typical minimums are 1-3 months for contracted reserved capacity, but for evaluation we can offer a 2-week reserved trial under a POC agreement (no long-term commit) -- we'll include that in the SOW. Pricing and any pilot discounts we'll surface once we finalize sizing.

Let me know the best time on July 20 to kick off and the contact email for the procurement thread.

Thanks --
